supporting_observations.claim: The repeated failed logons target svc-docsync and originate from FILE-MAP-01 at 10.53.20.20, using the same LSASS process and LogonType 3. The failures recur at roughly one-minute intervals from 13:35 through 13:50 UTC.
The domain-controller records report bad-password status for svc-docsync during this sequence, including 4776 status 0xc000006a and 4771 status 0x18.

The source host, target service account, and approximately one-minute retry cadence are consistent with the inventory's DocSync job on FILE-MAP-01, which runs every minute and re-authenticates, and with the scheduled svc-docsync password rotation at 13:30 UTC. This makes stale credentials in the job after rotation the most likely explanation for the alerted failures.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records show authentication failures but do not include the password-rotation execution, DocSync configuration update, or job/application logs that would confirm the operational cause.
The supplied records cover only the provided events; they do not establish whether successful svc-docsync authentications occurred elsewhere in the review window.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not prove that the scheduled password rotation completed at 13:30 UTC or that the DocSync job retained the old password.
The evidence does not establish whether any successful authentication or other activity involving svc-docsync occurred outside the supplied records.
unrelated_findings: Separate review recommended: at 14:18 UTC, WS-GLUND-01 recorded a SYSTEM-context PowerShell process using explicit credentials targeting svc-docsync on DC-MAP-01. This is distinct from the earlier repeated failures sourced from FILE-MAP-01; the record alone does not establish whether this use was authorized or connected. Record: T152-00037.
